entries.name: flatmap-nested-lie-accept#0
entries.script: { If(false, Coll(Coll(1)), Coll(Coll(2L))).flatMap({ (x: Coll[Int]) => x.indices }) }  // JVM: Coll(0). A Coll[Long] element satisfies the declared Coll[Int] because the lambda's argument check is SHALLOW (isValueOfType asks only isInstanceOf[Coll[_]] for a collection, SType.scala:198), and flatMap_eval reads no element type of its own. An implementation gating flatMap on the element type rejects this instead

entries.name: flatmap-empty-accept#1
entries.script: { If(false, Coll(Coll(1)), Coll[Coll[Long]]()).flatMap({ (x: Coll[Int]) => x.indices }) }  // JVM: an empty Coll — no element, so the lambda never runs and no check of any kind fires

entries.name: flatmap-long-element-errored#2
entries.script: { If(false, Coll(Coll(1)), Coll(2L)).flatMap({ (x: Coll[Int]) => x.indices }) }  // JVM: REJECTS. Here the element is a plain Long, and a Long is no Coll — the shallow check does stop this one. So flatMap's gate is not absent, it is just shallower than the node's declared element type
